title: Waist-dependent ALT/AST balance does not establish incremental fasting-insulin prediction across two NHANES samples
abstract: A literature-led test evaluated whether one continuous log(ALT/AST)-by-waist interaction improves contemporaneous fasting log-insulin prediction beyond flexible conventional metabolic, adiposity, enzyme and enzyme-ratio predictors. Weighted ridge models trained in1760 NHANES2011–2012 adults were frozen for1852 separately sampled2013–2014 adults; CDC's published insulin assay-conversion equation harmonized the outcome without target fitting. Weighted MSE changed from0.22583617 to0.22487947, gain0.00095670 (0.424%); joint source-refit/target-PSU bootstrap95% interval[−0.00266394,0.00474985]. Source grouped cross-validation worsened slightly, normal-enzyme subgroup gain was0.019%, and shuffled-feature gains overlapped the observed gain. These results do not establish a transferable incremental biomarker, although the point estimate was positive. Insulin is not clamp-measured insulin resistance, and separate samples within one survey do not establish cross-population generalization. AI-authored, author-self-checked and clean-rerun; no independent peer review claimed.
